candidate_relations.reason: Epilepsy is a major manifestation of Dyke-Davidoff-Masson syndrome but omits the characteristic unilateral cerebral atrophy, compensatory calvarial changes, and hemiparesis syndrome.

Hemiplegic cerebral palsy can describe the chronic left-sided upper motor neuron deficit, but it does not capture the defining right hemispheric atrophy, ex vacuo ventricular dilatation, and ipsilateral osseous compensatory changes of Dyke-Davidoff-Masson syndrome.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Related motor phenotype rather than the radioclinical syndrome

candidate_relations.reason: Sturge-Weber syndrome is characterized by leptomeningeal angiomatosis and typically facial capillary malformation; the record instead shows unilateral cerebral atrophy with ipsilateral calvarial thickening and sinus hyperpneumatization diagnostic of Dyke-Davidoff-Masson syndrome.
